maya: quick heads-up — ran the kernel_scheduler canary on mixtral-8x7b. performance looks weird: p50 ~ same, but p95/p99 jumped ~18% on long-context workloads (1.5k-2k). also seeing a small eval drop on qa-eval-2026.
priya: can you paste the exact canary tag and the config you used? :eyes:
maya: tag=runtime-canary-2026-03-16, kernel_scheduler=enabled, attention_policy=auto-swap, batch_strategy=continuous, kv_layout=optimized-copy
maya: perf snippet (local capture):
```
model=mixtral-8x7b | seq=2048 | qps=12
p50=45ms p95=210ms p99=380ms (baseline p99=320ms)
nvprof: memcpy_htoh ~ 28% runtime, kernel-memset ~ 9%, attention-kernelA ~ 31%
```
liam: memcpy spike is suspicious — did the new scheduler change kv cache ownership/copies? previous kernel used in-place KV layout, new kernel expects interleaved layout so we do a copy at swap time.
maya: yeah, profiler shows extra memcpy when we hit the kernel-swap branch at decode step ~8. Also noticed kv-cache size temporarily increases by ~20% and then GC/evict churn.
sasha: could that churn explain the quality delta? if kv pointers get reallocated mid-decode, the KV order for rope heads might be misaligned — subtle RoPE phase shift.
priya: we saw similar in qwen-tile work when switching tiled-attn kernel; the quant toggles didn't change tokens but ordering bugs did. @maya can you run the eval with deterministic seed and dump kv snapshot before/after swap?
maya: running now. attaching diff soon. also adding a canary that forces kernel_scheduler but disables layout-copy to isolate memcpy cost.
(devops-bot): deploy canary runtime-canary-2026-03-16 -> eng-runtime-canary started at 1790123500
maya: kv snapshot diff (summary):
```
- kv[0:64] hash=0x3f2a... -> kv[0:64] hash=0x3f2b... (offset +1)
- head-order mismatch at layer 10 for token idx 11
```
liam: that offset +1 screams RoPE scaling/stride mismatch. Did the scheduler swap to an attention kernel that assumes legacy RoPE scaling or a different head-dim packing?
maya: yes, kernel B assumes interleaved head-dims (h,row-major) vs kernel A (h,col-major). when we memcpy we didn't re-layout for RoPE, we just copied raw kv. So runtime swapped kernel + copy but forgot transform.
sasha: hmm okay bug is in kernel_scheduler's layout transformation step. Two potential fixes: (A) transform layout during copy to match target kernel (costly but correct), (B) restrict scheduler to only swap between kernels with the same layout (fast fallback). both require a rollback decision for stable.
priya: immediate mitigation: rollback scheduler for mixtral-8x7b and pin to kernel A for sequences >1024. also start a rollout that only allows swaps when seq<256 for now.
liam: agree. also add a regression test: run a short eval that checks kv snapshots equality after warmup for 5 seeds.
maya: I'm drafting revert PR to disable scheduler for affected models + add snapshot test. will post link.
(devops-bot): canary runtime-canary-2026-03-16 -> eng-runtime-canary deploy failed healthcheck at 1790123680 (rolling back)
maya: thanks bot. assigning rollback task to me. ETA ~ 2hrs to revert + run full eval suite.
sasha: add a postmortem note in incidents if eval dropout > 0.5% or perf regression persists after revert. also schedule a design review for making kernel metadata explicit (layout/rope-compat) so scheduler can check compatibility before swapping.
priya: created a quick ticket: INF-2142 "kernel_scheduler: add kernel capability matrix (layout/rope/quant-compatible)" and linked to this thread.
liam: one more note — when we reintroduce scheduler, prefer an A/B rollout that ties kernel selection to model config (head-dim, kv-layout) rather than runtime heuristics alone.
maya: agreed. wrapping up: reverting now, will update thread with PR id and eval numbers once done. :thumbsup:
